Subject: Authorization request: Senior SecEng offer above comp band (market data attached)

Team —

We completed onsite interviews for the Senior Security Engineer (REQ-1187). Candidate: Sofia Torres (linked resume and interview notes in Greenhouse). She has a strong infra security background (previous at a cloud infra company) and is a priority hire — immediate replacement for a departure and critical for our upcoming SOC scope expansion.

Request: I propose extending an offer with base salary at $200,000 (target band top is $180,000 for this grade). Total on-target comp (incl. 12% bonus) ~ $224k. This is above the current band by ~11%.

Rationale:
- Market: comparable Senior SecEng roles at cloud companies are bidding in the $190–215k range for Bay Area hires; Q3 market packet attached.
- Candidate: rare blend of infra + compliance automation; candidate would own encryption and key rotation program and a new runbook framework which we currently lack.
- Cost of delay: if we lose this candidate, projected time-to-fill is 4–6 months. That gap adds risk to SOC timeline and potential contractor spend.

Asks:
1) Compensation exception approval (base > band) OR permission to move to hiring band + signing bonus to bridge.
2) Confirmation that headcount remains available for REQ-1187 (hiring plan says reserved but I want explicit HC sign-off).
3) If approved, signoff on offer authority and docuSign owner.

Attachments: q3-2026-govsec-market-bands.pdf; candidate-salary-calibration.xlsx; req-REQ-1187-justification.docx

Thanks — Vivek

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Security & Compliance

Vivek —

Thanks for the packet. I reviewed the candidate's comp expectation and Greenfield confirms they're firm on $200k base (negotiable by $5k at most). Our calibrated band for this grade ends at $180k. Two options to close quickly:

1) Approve exception for $200k base. We will need written approval from Comp (Marissa) and HC confirmation from Laura. If Comp approves, payroll needs coding and offer owner identified for docuSign.
2) Keep base at band top $180k and offer a $20k sign-on paid over 12 months + accelerated LTI (subject to executive signoff). This keeps base aligned with band but increases near-term cash impact.

Notes: candidate indicated they will wait for a firm offer until 11/6 — we have limited runway. I recommend we prioritize speed.

Action items: Marissa / Laura — can you advise preferred path and confirm whether we can make an exception? If we go with exception, Marissa, we need comp exception memo and Laura please confirm HC is available against the Q4 hiring plan.

Cheers — Neha

Neha / Vivek —

Thanks for the detailed note. I ran the market packet against our internal comp model. A few points:

- The candidate profile does align with the high end of Senior ICs. External market shows $195–215k for similar companies in the Bay Area.
- Comp exception policy allows up to +10% above band for critical hires with strong justification and VP signoff. This request (~11%) is slightly above that threshold.

Options I recommend (fastest path):
A) Approve base exception to $198k (midpoint between band cap and ask), plus a $10k one-time sign-on to reach candidate expectation. We limit precedent by adding a requirement for documented deliverables (defined OKRs for 6 months) and flagging hire in the quarterly comp exception register.
B) Maintain $180k base + $30k sign-on (front-loaded 50% at 30 days). This keeps baseline discipline but increases cash outlay.

If leadership prefers to fully meet the ask at $200k base, I can draft the comp exception memo and escalate to EVP/Finance for approval — that will add ~2 business days.

Please indicate which path you prefer. If you pick A or full exception, I will prepare the formal exception memo and route to Finance for final sign-off.

-Marissa
